# Home Environment Manager Beta 102 — native thermal PID ON follow-through

Based exactly on validated Beta 101.

**Fixed:** A physical heating/cooling climate entity can acknowledge a
HEAT/COOL mode with its previous 4–5°C antifrost target. The previous binary
PID implementation waited until the end of the ordinary control tick to
correct it; when the PID entered an OFF phase but the already-running output
was still inside its mandatory minimum ON, that tick returned before it ever
applied the native maximum for heating or minimum for cooling.

- When PID demand is positive, a native climate is **confirmed in the requested
  mode and still HEM-owned**, HEM now prioritizes its existing native setpoint
  command and feedback acknowledgment before an unrelated minimum-ON hold can
  starve it.
- The physical entity's live `max_temp` (heat) and `min_temp` (cool), with its
  own `target_temp_step`, remain authoritative. These are separate from the
  room comfort target, which continues to govern PID demand.
- The fix never writes a setpoint to an OFF device, does not adopt a physically
  running unowned thermostat, does not delay an already-permitted OFF, and does
  not bypass startup, window, sleeping, heating/cooling conflict, compressor
  dwell, physical ACK, or native/manual override gates.
- Existing/Manual and normal native thermostatic control are untouched.
- New source-based PID/HA simulation covers stale 5°C active heating,
  4°C cooling minima, the OFF-phase minimum ON hold, permitted OFF, satisfied
  demand, missing HEM ownership, windows, and non-PID mode.
- Full Beta101 inherited backend + browser regression and HACS packaging
  are run again before publication.

This is a guarded universal fix, not a per-device option or hard-coded workaround.
It is not a claim that any live thermostat has been operated or verified.
